from.place: ## Proof, step (b) Essential surjectivity: algebraization through formal glueing, specifically the torsion-extension descent used in Proposition 05ER

title: Extension descent assembles from summands of the quotient
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a flat map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $N$ an $R$-module and $(C_j)_{j\in J}$ any family of $R$-modules. Put $P=\bigoplus_{j\in J}C_j$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. Assume that for each $j$ every $S$-module extension $0\to N\otimes_RS\to T_j\to C_j\otimes_RS\to0$ is isomorphic, with its end terms fixed, to the base change of an $R$-module extension $0\to N\to E_j\to C_j\to0$. Then every $S$-module extension $0\to N\otimes_RS\to T\to P\otimes_RS\to0$ is likewise isomorphic, with its end terms fixed, to the base change of an $R$-module extension $0\to N\to E\to P\to0$ [def-weil-module-base-change], [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. The family $J$ need not be finite.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 05EG (lemma-neighbourhood-extensions, line 24516): 'Using compatibility of Ext with direct sums (details omitted) we reduce to the case where M = R/I^n'

proof.text: For each $j$, put $f_j=1_S\otimes\iota_j$ and $r_j=1_S\otimes\pi_j$. Their composite is the identity, by base change compatibility with composition. Define $T_j=b^{-1}(\operatorname{im}f_j)$ as a submodule of $T$, with injection $a_j(n)=a(n)$ and quotient $b_j(t)=r_j(b(t))$. Membership gives $f_j(r_j(b(t)))=b(t)$. Injectivity of $a_j$ follows from that of $a$; exactness follows from the displayed identity and exactness of $a,b$; surjectivity follows by lifting $f_j(c)$ through $b$. Thus $T_j$ is in the same universe as $T$ and the summand hypothesis applies. Choose its descended extension $N\to E_j\to C_j$ and equivalence. Compose the equivalence with $T_j\hookrightarrow T$ to obtain $k_j:S\otimes E_j\to T$, with $k_j(1\otimes i_j)=a$ and $bk_j=(1\otimes\iota_j)(1\otimes q_j)$.

Apply only the surjectivity clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ext-one-direct-sum] over $R$ to the extensions $E_j$. Obtain an extension $N\xrightarrow{i}F\xrightarrow{q}\bigoplus C_j$ and fixed-endpoint isomorphisms from its pullbacks to $E_j$. Their inverse maps followed by first projection give maps $f_j:E_j\to F$ satisfying $f_ji_j=i$ and $qf_j=\iota_jq_j$.

Regard $T$ as an $R$-module. Write $a_0(n)=a(1\otimes n)$ and $t_j(e)=k_j(1\otimes e)$. Prove the gluing assertion directly: the map $p:N\oplus\bigoplus E_j\to F$, $(n,d)\mapsto i(n)+\sum_j f_j(d_j)$, is surjective, since the direct sum of the $q_j$ is surjective and $\ker q=\operatorname{im}i$. If $p(n,d)=0$, then every $q_j(d_j)=0$, so $d$ is in the image of $\bigoplus i_j$. Write $d=(i_j(n_j))_j$. Then injectivity of $i$ gives $n+\sum_jn_j=0$, and consequently $a_0(n)+\sum_jt_j(d_j)=0$. Thus the map to $T$ factors through $F\cong(N\oplus\bigoplus E_j)/\ker p$, yielding $g_0:F\to T$ with $g_0i=a_0$ and $g_0f_j=t_j$. Extend scalars by the explicit tensor lift $g(s\otimes e)=s\,g_0(e)$. Maps from $F$ agreeing on $i(N)$ and all $f_j(E_j)$ agree: the same surjectivity argument writes every element as $i(n)+\sum_j f_j(d_j)$. Apply this to get $bg_0(e)=1\otimes q(e)$, hence $g(1\otimes i)=a$ and $bg=1\otimes q$. All sums have finite support; the argument works for arbitrary, including empty, $J$.

Flat tensor exactness [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] gives $\ker(1\otimes q)=\operatorname{im}(1\otimes i)$; tensor right exactness [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] gives surjectivity of $1\otimes q$. If $g(x)=0$, then $(1\otimes q)(x)=0$, so $x=(1\otimes i)(n)$ and $a(n)=0$. Injectivity of $a$ forces $n=0$ and $x=0$. For any $t\in T$, choose $x$ with $(1\otimes q)(x)=b(t)$. Exactness of $a,b$ gives $t-g(x)=a(n)$, so $g(x+(1\otimes i)(n))=t$. Thus $g$ is bijective and defines the required fixed-endpoint linear equivalence.

proof_origin.note: Explicit gluing argument filling the direct-sum compatibility omitted in Stacks Tag 05EG; retains Ext-one surjectivity but replaces tensor-pullback comparison and Ext-one injectivity by a quotient factorization and an elementwise short-five-lemma argument. Source: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 05EG (lemma-neighbourhood-extensions).
